QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_30

question.text: Himadri Growth Fund's unliquidated portfolio is valued at INR 120 crore. The Manager arranges bids totalling INR 24 crore for in-specie distribution purposes. At what value will the unliquidated investments be distributed in-specie?

answer.text: INR 24 crore (bid value, because bids are ≥ 25% threshold).
INR 120 crore (full NAV, because bids are arranged).
ONE RUPEE (because INR 24 crore bids are below the 25% of INR 120 crore = INR 30 crore threshold).

explanation.text: The Logic: 25% of INR 120 crore = INR 30 crore. The bids arranged (INR 24 crore) are BELOW this 25% threshold. Per workbook pp.296-297: distribution is at bid value if bids are arranged for at least 25% of unliquidated-investment value, and ONE RUPEE if that threshold is not met. Since INR 24 crore < INR 30 crore, the keyed One Rupee answer applies for performance-benchmarking purposes. The Trap: Distributing at the shortfall bid value (Option A) ignores the threshold rule. Full NAV (Option B) is never the fallback. INR 30 crore (Option C) is an invented 'floor' — the rule is binary: bid value (if at or above 25%) OR One Rupee. Note: The in-specie distribution rule is binary — if bids reach at least 25% of unliquidated-investment value, distribute at bid value; otherwise the investments are recorded at One Rupee for performance benchmarking.
